headline: Easy-run cardiac drift has dropped meaningfully while weekly volume continues to build — aerobic efficiency is visibly improving.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your aerobic system is responding. Easy-run heart rate has fallen noticeably across comparable efforts compared to the prior period, which — alongside continued volume growth — is one of the clearest in-training signals of genuine aerobic adaptation rather than just accumulated mileage. The 18 km effort on July 4th slots in as your longest recent run and contributes to a block that's now running meaningfully ahead of the prior four weeks, without any apparent cost to recovery quality or pace.

The lactate threshold test from July 2nd gives a useful anchor point. With only one test in the current 30-day window, it's a single data point rather than a trend — but the pace is credible relative to your half-marathon and 10K history, and worth treating as a working baseline to track against.

Strength frequency has edged slightly lower this block. Not a concern in isolation, but worth keeping an eye on as running volume builds — your strength profile is a genuine asset and the two qualities are complementary rather than competing.
watch_items: Watch whether easy-run HR continues its downward trend or plateaus — a further drop would confirm the adaptation is consolidating
Monitor how strength session frequency holds up as running load increases heading into the next block
The lactate threshold test is currently a single reference point — note whether threshold-adjacent efforts feel easier or harder relative to July 2nd
With the running streak now matching your personal best at 20 weeks, observe how freshness and motivation track over the coming 7–10 days

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 145 km vs 125 km prior block (+16%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 146 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
